summary: OrionHealth - EU-WEST production: sustained 5xx + routing anomaly causing inconsistent fallback outputs and unexpected billing spike
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-09 12:42 UTC and 2026-03-09 14:20 UTC OrionHealth observed sustained 5xx errors on streaming RPCs and REST generation endpoints in eu-west. Simultaneously, a subset of routed requests were bounced to an older quantized variant (rw-7b-quantized) which produced short, truncated responses and higher token counts resulting in a billing anomaly. Customer impact: OrionHealth reported degraded clinical-search UX, several timed-out autocomplete requests, and an unexpected daily bill increase. They opened an escalation with CSM at 12:51 UTC.
impact: Customer-facing production outage in eu-west for OrionHealth. High error rate (~18% 5xx on generation endpoints), increased tail latency, truncated streaming responses for specific routes, and ~30% higher token usage for affected requests during the window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use OrionHealth prod API key and call /v1/generate (model pinned to 'rw-13b-v2') with long-context clinical prompt (context ~2k tokens)
2) Observe that ~1 in 5 requests return 5xx or stream disconnects between 12:42-13:40 UTC in eu-west
3) For a subset of traffic routed under policy 'cost-fallback', requests are routed to rw-7b-quantized producing truncated completions and higher token emission patterns
4) Reproduce rate by running 200 concurrent short-stream connections from eu-west region
timeline: 2026-03-09 12:42 UTC - First alert: elevated 5xx rate on eu-west generator (internal monitoring)
2026-03-09 12:51 UTC - Customer (OrionHealth CSM) reports user-facing failures; ticket opened and escalated to P0
2026-03-09 13:05 UTC - Mitigation applied: emergency routing rule to prefer rw-13b-v2 explicit pin for OrionHealth; partial traffic moved off cost-fallback path
2026-03-09 13:18 UTC - SRE discovered spike in failure to the kernel selection service for eu-west edge; retries caused cascade and fallback routing engaged
2026-03-09 13:45 UTC - Rolling restart of kernel-selection pod group in eu-west; 5xx rate drops to baseline over next 20 minutes
2026-03-09 14:20 UTC - All traffic stable on rw-13b-v2; customer reports service restored; ticket escalated to post-incident follow-up
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor or GPU OOM in dedicated pool — verified no OOMs in infra metrics for customer nodes

Kernel selection service (router) in eu-west returned intermittent 502 when under high threading contention; these 502s propagated up and triggered cost-fallback policy which preferred quantized variants
Logs show backpressure on kernel-selection: increased RPC latency to model-chooser service from 35ms baseline to 450ms during peak
A retry loop in the routing layer used an exponential backoff that inadvertently amplified concurrent requests to kernel-selection, producing a short-lived cascade
Billing anomaly root: rw-7b-quantized produced more short-prompt tokens for medical templates due to different EOS handling; combined with retries this increased billed tokens per user session
mitigation_and_workaround: Applied emergency routing override to pin customer to rw-13b-v2 for OrionHealth (policy change) at 13:05 UTC
Scaled kernel-selection replicas + increased request queueing buffer in eu-west to absorb bursts
Disabled automatic cost-fallback routing for enterprise customers by default (temporary) to prevent unintended model variants
Provided customer with a temporary billing credit for the incident window and opened billing review (finance notified)
resolution_summary: Root cause was a transient contention and retry amplification in the kernel-selection/routing layer in eu-west which caused 502/5xx propagation and engagement of cost-fallback paths. Mitigations included routing override, scaling kernel-selection, and disabling enterprise cost-fallback. Service returned to normal by 14:20 UTC. Billing credit issued and follow-up engineering changes planned.
